Outcome_variable.evidence_source: [page/1/Text/1] Rigby and Huebner (2005) did not found any relation between Extraversion and life satisfaction. Rigby and Huebner (2005) suggested that specific avoidant behavior (e.g., avoiding standing out) in some adolescents might reduce the advantages of Extraversion we see among adults. Moreover, Diener and Seligman (2002) found that Extraversion, among other factors, is recurrent in both very happy and very unhappy adults. This has lead to the conclusion that Extraversion seems to be necessary but not sufficient for high levels of happiness (Diener and Seligman 2002).
Outcome_variable.warning: The study aims to address 'happiness' and mentions 'life satisfaction' in the context of previous research. Assuming 'happiness' refers to life satisfaction or a general SWB measure.
